title: Grade 4 French — Thu, May 21
description: Les articles — Day 4 of 5: Partitive articles (du, de la, de l', des)
subject: french

questions.question: What is a partitive article used for?
options: Referring to an unspecified PART of something (some/any)
questions.explanation: Partitive articles express 'some' or 'any' of an uncountable substance. Je mange du pain = I eat some bread.

questions.question: What is the partitive article for MASCULINE nouns?
questions.explanation: 'Du' = partitive for masculine (du pain, du café, du riz). Du is a contraction of 'de + le'.

questions.question: What is the partitive article for FEMININE nouns?
questions.explanation: 'De la' = partitive for feminine (de la soupe, de la viande, de la tarte).

questions.question: What partitive article is used before a noun starting with a vowel?
questions.explanation: 'De l'' is used before vowels (both genders). De l'eau (water, fem.), de l'air (air, masc.).

questions.question: Fill in: 'Je bois ___ café.' (I drink some coffee — masculine)
questions.explanation: 'Je bois du café.' = I drink coffee. Café is masculine → du.

questions.question: Fill in: 'Elle mange ___ soupe.' (she eats some soup — feminine)
questions.explanation: 'Elle mange de la soupe.' = She eats soup. Soupe is feminine → de la.

questions.question: Fill in: 'Il boit ___ eau.' (he drinks some water — feminine, vowel start)
questions.explanation: 'Il boit de l'eau.' = He drinks water. Eau is feminine and starts with vowel → de l'.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'du pain' and 'le pain'?
options: Du pain = some bread (unspecified amount); Le pain = THE bread (specific loaf)
Le pain = some bread; du pain = the bread
questions.explanation: Du pain = partitive (some/any bread). Le pain = definite (the specific bread). Context determines which to use.

questions.question: Translate: 'I eat some rice.' (riz = rice, masculine)
questions.explanation: 'Je mange du riz.' = I eat some rice. Riz is masculine → du.

questions.question: After negation, du/de la/des → :
questions.explanation: After negation (ne...pas), ALL partitive articles → de/d'. Je mange du pain → Je ne mange pas de pain.

questions.question: Complete: 'Je mange ___ viande et je bois ___ jus.' (some meat/masc, some juice/masc)
options: de la viande / de la jus
questions.explanation: Viande (meat) is feminine → de la viande. Jus (juice) is masculine → du jus.

questions.question: Which sentence is WRONG?
questions.explanation: 'De la riz' is wrong — riz is masculine, so it should be 'du riz'. Nous mangeons DU riz.

questions.question: All three article types for 'un repas complet' (a complete meal): bread, water, salad:
options: du pain, de l'eau, de la salade
un pain, une eau, une salade
des pain, des eau, des salade
questions.explanation: Du pain (masc), de l'eau (fem, vowel), de la salade (fem) — partitive articles showing some of each.

questions.question: Translate: 'She doesn't eat meat.'
options: Elle ne mange pas de la viande.
Elle ne mange pas de viande.
Elle ne mange pas du viande.
questions.explanation: 'Elle ne mange pas de viande.' After negation (ne...pas), de la → de.

questions.question: Summary: which is the partitive article?
questions.explanation: Partitive = du (masc), de la (fem), de l' (before vowel), des (plural). Used for 'some/any' of an uncountable.
